title: Centralized vs Distributed
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1a · Section 1-1 · Version control systems Centralized vs Distributed With Git, every computer holds the whole history. GitHub is a copy you share, not the only copy. Where does the history live? online Centralized Distributed (Git) Switch the mode, then click the server to take it offline. The one idea Centralized: one copy of the history, so when the server is down nobody commits. Distributed: a full copy on every computer. Git is distributed. GitHub is the copy you share; commits work offline and you push when you are back. That is why you commit on your machine first and push second.

title: Compile, Bytecode, JVM
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 2-1 · Compiling Java Compile, Bytecode, JVM javac checks it and turns it into bytecode once; a JVM on any computer runs that same bytecode. Source Focus HelloWorld.java source text javac HelloWorld.java javac the Java compiler HelloWorld.class target/classes/com/pluralsight the same .class, copied to any computer step 0 / 8 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · the source is HelloWorld.java. Try missing semicolon. HelloWorld.java .class file ? Runs on ? The one idea javac turns source into bytecode once , and only when the grammar is right. The JVM runs that bytecode anywhere : the same HelloWorld.class works on a Mac, a Windows PC and a Linux machine. A syntax error stops at javac: no .class, nothing to run .

title: JDK, JRE, JVM
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 2-1 · The Java platform JDK, JRE, JVM Three names that nest inside each other. Pick what you want to do and watch which layer lights up. One inside the other JDK Java Development Kit For writing programs. The tools a developer needs, plus a JRE inside so you can test what you wrote. javac compiler debugger javadoc jar tool JRE Java Runtime Environment For running programs. The class libraries your code calls, plus the JVM that executes it. No compiler. java.lang java.util java.io class libraries JVM Java Virtual Machine The engine. Loads a .class file and executes its bytecode. One JVM per kind of computer, so the same .class runs anywhere. class loader bytecode interpreter garbage collector you need JDK Write a Java program Run a Java program Just execute bytecode IntelliJ uses the JDK you installed, Amazon Corretto 17 . So you already have all three layers. The one idea JVM runs bytecode. JRE is the JVM plus the class libraries: enough to run. JDK is the JRE plus the tools: needed to write. Install a JDK and you get all three; install only a JRE and you can run programs but never compile one.

title: final Constants
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-1 · Read-only variables final Constants Flip final on and the line that tries to change it no longer compiles. Main.java 1 final String myName = "Raymond" ; 2 System.out.println( "Your name is: " + myName); 3 myName = myName + " Maroun" ; Cannot assign a value to final variable 'myName' 4 System.out.println( "The full name is: " + myName); The variable String myName final off final off final on A value fixed for every run is a constant, named in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE : final int DAYS_IN_WEEK = 7; The one idea final means assign once. The compiler stops any later change before the program ever runs, which is why constants like DAYS_IN_WEEK are declared final.

title: Naming Conventions
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-1 · Naming conventions and consistency Naming Conventions Click any name in the code and see what kind of thing it is and which rule shaped it. Names Real names from this week package com.pluralsight ; import java.util . Scanner ; public class Main { public static void main ( String [] args ) { final int DAYS_IN_WEEK = 7; int firstNumber = 26; boolean isStudent = true ; Scanner myScanner = new Scanner (System.in); String firstName = myScanner . nextLine (); String lastName = myScanner . nextLine (); String fullName = generateFullName ( firstName , lastName ); } public static int addNumbers ( int num1 , int num2 ) { return num1 + num2 ; } public static String generateFullName ( String firstName , String lastName ) { return firstName + " " + lastName ; } } The five shapes Class PascalCase Main, HelloWorld, Scanner Variable camelCase firstNumber, isStudent Method camelCase() addNumbers, generateFullName Constant (final) UPPER_SNAKE_CASE DAYS_IN_WEEK Package all.lowercase com.pluralsight The compiler accepts first_number or main_class . Nobody writes them, so they stand out as wrong. The one idea The shape of a name tells the reader what it is before they read the code. The compiler does not enforce these rules, but every Java developer follows them, so a name in the wrong shape reads as a mistake.

title: Concatenation vs Addition
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-2 · String concatenation Concatenation vs Addition In Java, + has two jobs. Between two numbers it adds; the moment a String is on either side, it glues text together. Pick an expression Focus How Java reads the line, one + at a time number + number → addition String + anything → concatenation step 0 / 6 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Try all three. Main.java this + means ? result type ? console The one idea + becomes concatenation the moment a String is on either side , and Java works left to right, one + at a time. So "Sum: " + 1 + 2 prints Sum: 12, while 1 + 2 + " apples" prints 3 apples. Put parentheses around the math you want done first: "Sum: " + (1 + 2) prints Sum: 3.

title: Integer Division and Modulo
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-2 · Operators and expressions Integer Division and Modulo When both sides are int, 10 / 3 is 3: the leftover is cut off, and % hands that leftover back. Numbers Focus step 0 / 9 Press Next . The picture changes at every step. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · try 1 and 2 Main.java a / b ? a % b ? console The one idea int divided by int gives an int. Java keeps the whole groups and throws the leftover away. It cuts, it never rounds, so 10 / 3 is 3 and 1 / 2 is 0. % gives you the leftover that / dropped: 10 % 3 is 1. Make both sides double and the leftover counts as a fraction of a group instead.

title: Pre and Post Increment
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-2 · Pre/post increment and decrement Pre and Post Increment With y = x++ y gets the old value, with y = ++x y gets the new one. Pick the statement Focus copy of the value x · int 5 was 5 y · int no value read x: 5 +1 5 press Next step 0 / 5 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Run one, then the other. Main.java y gets ? x ends at ? console The one idea Both x++ and ++x add 1 to x. The position of ++ decides what y gets: after x, y gets the value before the increment (5); before x, y gets the value after it (6). x-- and --x work the same way, subtracting 1.

title: Widening, Narrowing, Casting
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-2 · Literals are typed, widening, narrowing, casting Widening, Narrowing, Casting A value moves into a bigger type on its own, but into a smaller one only with a cast, and whatever does not fit is lost. Pick an example Focus Each type is a cup. Bigger cup, wider range of values step 0 / 6 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next Main.java from ? to ? Output console The one idea Java widens for free; narrowing needs a cast and you own whatever is lost. Along byte, short, int, long, float, double, moving right is automatic. Moving left does not compile until you write the cast, and then Java drops digits ( 123.4567890123 becomes 123.45679 ), cuts decimals ( (int) 9.99 is 9) or wraps around ( (int) 3000000000L is -1294967296), with no error and no warning.

title: printf Format Specifiers
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-3 · Formatting output printf Format Specifiers Each % placeholder takes the next argument, in order, and the letters after the % say how that value is written. Pick a printf line Focus Placeholders and arguments, matched in order The line printf builds step 0 / 6 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · dots in the output are spaces added to reach the width. Try the width line. Main.java placeholder ? takes argument ? console The one idea Placeholders are filled left to right from the arguments: the 1st % takes the 1st argument, the 2nd takes the 2nd. The letter after % says how to format the value: s text, d whole number, f decimal. A number before it sets the width (a minus means left aligned), .2 sets two decimals, a comma groups digits, and %n ends the line.

title: Scanner Methods
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-3 · Reading input with Scanner Scanner Methods Each Scanner method takes a different piece of the typed line: one word, the whole line, or one number. text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 3-3 · Buffered input and line separators Scanner Buffer nextInt() takes the digits and leaves the line separator behind, so the next nextLine() returns an empty String without waiting. Another nextInt() skips it, but nextLine() reads up to it, finds nothing, and returns "". When you read a number and then a line, consume the leftover first with an extra myScanner.nextLine() .

title: if / else Path
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-1 and 4-3 · if, else if, else, and the conditional operator if / else Path Java checks the conditions top to bottom, runs the block of the first one that is true, and skips the rest. The age the user typed Focus step 0 / 5 ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Try 15: it is also under 65. Main.java age ? price ? console The one idea Java checks the conditions in order, runs the first true one, and skips the rest , even a later condition that would also be true. else has no condition: it catches whatever is left. cond ? a : b is the same choice written as a value : double price = (age < 18) ? 22.50 : 25.00;

title: Logical Operators
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-1 · Logical operators Logical Operators Java reads the condition left to right and stops as soon as the answer is known. Pick the values Focus How Java reads the condition left ? not checked right ? whole condition ? if block else block step 0 / 7 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Try age 12, then age 30. Main.java left side ? right side ? console The one idea && needs both sides true, || needs one, ! flips true and false. Java reads left to right and stops as soon as the answer is known : a false left side settles an && , a true left side settles an || , and the right side is never checked.

title: == vs .equals
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-1 · Comparing Strings == vs .equals == checks whether two arrows point at the same object; .equals checks whether the characters match. Where do the two Strings come from? Focus step 0 / 5 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Try two literals. Main.java name == expected ? .equals ? console The one idea == asks "same object?", .equals asks "same characters?" Text the user types is a new object, so == against a literal is false even when the words match. Two identical literals share one pooled object, which is why == sometimes seems to work. For text you almost always mean .equals , or .equalsIgnoreCase when capital letters should not matter.

title: Method Signature
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-2 · Static methods Method Signature It says what you must pass, in what order, and what you get back, and every call has to match it. Pick a method Focus Main.java, inside class Main step 0 / 8 Press Next to start. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · Try greetUser for void. You must pass ? You get back ? The one idea The header is a contract. The parameter list says what you must pass and in what order: each argument must have its parameter's type, and the names do not have to match. The return type says what comes back and what you can store it in; void means nothing comes back.

title: Method Call Stack
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-2 · Static methods Method Call Stack Java builds a new box, runs the method there, then throws the box away. Step through it and watch the boxes stack up and come down. The call stack Focus nothing running yet step 0 / 0 Press Step to start the program, or Run to watch it play. Step → Run ← Back Reset Experiment: change num1 inside addNumbers space = step · the experiment adds a line that writes to the parameter. Does main's firstNumber change? Main.java Inputs · what main starts with main's variables firstNumber secondNumber firstName lastName Edit while stopped. The run below is computed from these, not replayed. frames on stack ? deepest so far ? console The one idea Every call gets its own frame with its own copies of the values. Parameters are copies, not links: changing num1 inside addNumbers leaves firstNumber in main untouched. The only thing that comes back is the return value, and the frame is gone the moment it returns.

title: Repeated Code to One Method
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-2 · Why methods Repeated Code to One Method Pull the repeated lines into one method, turn the numbers into parameters, and call it: main gets shorter, and a fix in one place reaches every call. The program so far Focus Main.java Output console step 0 / 8 Press Next to start. The code and the console change at every step. ← Back Next → Reset space = next · fixed sizes instead of Scanner input. lines in main ? copies of the code ? The one idea Write it once, name it, call it. When the same lines show up again and again, move them into a method, turn the values that change into parameters, and replace each copy with a call. main reads like a list of what happens, and a change in one place reaches every call . The workbook calls this D.R.Y.: Don't Repeat Yourself.

title: One Scanner, Three Ways
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-2 · Using a Scanner in multiple methods One Scanner, Three Ways Three ways to let methods read the keyboard. Same program, same output; only where the Scanner lives changes. The third wins. Pick a way Focus way 3 / 3 click a column · 1, 2, 3 on the keyboard ScannerAsParameter.java Scanner objects doAdd says it reads input verdict The one idea One Scanner per program, created in main, handed to each method as a parameter. A static field also gives one object, but hides who reads input and lets one close() cut everyone off. A Scanner per method gives several objects on one keyboard, and what one reads ahead the others never see.

title: switch, Both Forms
text: ← Week 1 index Workbook 1c · Section 4-3 · The switch statement switch, Both Forms In the traditional form it keeps running until it hits a break ; in the arrow form it runs one branch and stops. Pick a version Focus Traditional case 3: Arrow case 3 -> step 0 / 6 ← Back Next → Reset space = next · the day-of-week switch, with the learner typing 3. Try the break removed. dayNumber ? dayName ? console The one idea Both forms jump straight to the case that matches, and default catches every value no case names. The traditional form keeps running down the cases until it reaches a break , so a missing break lets the next case run too. The arrow form runs only its own branch and stops: no break, no fall-through.

Enter checks the line · type end when nothing more prints · capitals and extra spaces do not count · a double prints with a decimal point (25.0) The one idea A loop asks its question again before every pass. while and for ask first, so they can run zero times; do/while asks after, so it always runs once. break leaves the loop now; continue skips the rest of this pass and goes on to the next.

title: break or continue
desc: Fill the one blank that makes the loop print the target, then watch the real output.
text: ← Week 2 index Workbook 2a · Section 3-1 · Game break or continue Pick the piece that makes the loop print exactly the target. Then the loop runs, and you see what it really printed. Game loop score 0 time 0.0s target your loop printed Next break or continue Each round is one loop with one blank and the output it should print. Pick the piece that fills the blank, by click or keys 1 to 3. The loop then runs with your piece. Start Round over Play again round 0 / 12 Press Start . Keys 1 to 3 answer. break leaves the whole loop · continue skips the rest of this pass · % 3 == 0 true at 3, 6, 9 · == 3 true once · space or Enter goes on after a miss The one idea break ends the loop; continue ends only the current pass. After break, nothing else in the loop runs. After continue, the update runs and the loop checks its condition again, so the next pass still happens.
